analysis:
The only change is in scripts/test-provider-release-pipeline.py, head lines 180-185 (test_only_the_release_lane_compiles_the_release_environment). The base test asserted that the qualify-sdk job never mentions DARKBLOOM_RELEASE_ENVIRONMENT. The head test now expects qualify-sdk to set it exactly once, as a job-level env value of literal 'prod'. It is not the resolved-environment selector, and there is no step or shell override. build-provider still must use the resolved environment selector, and the signing job still smoke-checks the ENV_PREFIX/CLI_NAME build-environment string.

This is a test-only change with no runtime, credential, attestation or key-handling code. No secrets, signing, publication or trust-gate logic is modified in the supplied evidence. The test hardens the pipeline by pinning the qualification lane's compile environment, so a qualification build cannot silently pick up a dev or staging environment. It still asserts that qualify-sdk has no secrets and no environment approval (lines 167-175, unchanged).

The corresponding workflow change in .github/workflows/release-provider.yml and the action are not in the supplied units. I could not verify that the workflow matches the new assertion or that qualification with a 'prod' compile environment cannot affect a published artifact. The qualification lane's output is not signed or published, per the existing DAG tests, but that is outside the supplied evidence. No threat model asset (A-011, A-017, T-034, T-054) is demonstrably regressed by this test edit. No findings.
